subject: Clarification: training-on-data assurance + retention TTL exceptions for FinHealth
messages:
From: Diane Park <security@finhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: FinHealth Legal <legal@finhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: written assurance that Redwood does not train on customer content + retention specifics

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team is working through the vendor questionnaire and we have a couple of follow-ups specific to model training and retention before we loop legal in for contracting. Please can you confirm the following in writing for our audit: 

1) Does Redwood ever use customer-provided text (API inputs, uploaded files, transcripts) to train or fine-tune models used in production? If not, please explain how training data pipelines are isolated from customer data.

2) What data retention categories apply to hosted API customers vs. Dedicated vs. Private deployments (backups, snapshots, debug traces, logs, KV caches)? Include default TTLs and whether customers can shorten them (e.g., to 7 days).

3) For backups/snapshots: are there tombstone/archival copies that persist beyond the TTL? If so, what is the deletion workflow and typical timelines for final disposal?

4) Can you provide a signed attestation or SOC2 evidence that covers the no-training commitment and retention controls?

I've attached our short security questionnaire and highlighted the training/retention rows. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Diane Park
Dir., Information Security
FinHealth

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: written assurance that Redwood does not train on customer content + retention specifics

Hi Diane —

Thanks for the clear questions and for sending the questionnaire. Short answer up front: we do not use customer content to train or fine-tune our public production models by default. Below is a concise breakdown, followed by attachments and a technical follow-up from our infra team (cc'd).

1) Training usage
- Hosted API: customer inputs are isolated from our model training pipelines. We may collect aggregated, anonymized telemetry for service quality, but that data is not incorporated into model training. Any use of customer data for model improvement would require explicit customer opt-in and a contractual Addendum.
- Dedicated capacity: data remains within the dedicated tenant and is not used for Redwood model training.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer data never leaves the customer-controlled environment; Redwood does not access it for training.

2) Retention categories and defaults
- Request logs (request metadata, timestamps): default TTL 90 days for hosted to support billing and rate-limit enforcement; can be shortened via contract for enterprise/Dedicated.
- Debug snapshots and traces: default TTL 30 days; snapshots are ephemeral and retained only for troubleshooting; customers can request accelerated purge.
- Backups/snapshots: persisted snapshots are retained according to the deployment tier; default archival TTL is 180 days for hosted; Dedicated/Private can opt for shorter windows.
- KV caches and prefix caches: ephemeral in-memory caches; they do not persist beyond the lifecycle of the worker process; no durable training input flows from KV caches.

3) Tombstone/archive handling
- When a delete request is processed we tombstone the primary records immediately and schedule purge jobs against backups/archive indexes. Final disposal timelines vary by storage provider and region, but typical complete deletion is 7–45 days depending on replication windows. Our erase runbook outlines the purge workflow (link below).

4) Evidence and attestation
- We can provide a signed "No-Model-Training" attestation and SOC 2 Type II reports covering our controls; see attached attestation.pdf. If you need DocuSign, we can generate that.

I've attached our short attestation and a runbook excerpt for the delete flow. Priyom/Mina — could you add any infra specifics (KV cache lifecycle, snapshot retention mechanics, and whether we can commit to a 7-day TTL for FinHealth hosted logs)?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman

Subject: Re: Request: written assurance that Redwood does not train on customer content + retention specifics

Hi Diane / Naomi — quick technical details to supplement Naomi's note: 

- Isolation & training pipelines: our training infra is strictly separated. Customer data is stored in tenant-isolated buckets; ingestion pipelines for model training run from vetted public datasets and curated internal corpora. No automated export path exists from customer buckets into training stores.

- KV caches: leader-follower in-memory caches are per-tenant, kept in RAM or on local ephemeral NVMe; when workers restart the cache is rebuilt from upstream stores. No long-lived cache is fed into training.

- Snapshots & backups: nightly snapshots are incremental. For hosted customers the default snapshot retention is 180 days, but snapshots after a delete request are marked and queued for purge. The underlying object store enforces eventual deletion — replication and cross-region retention can extend final purge up to ~45 days. For Dedicated we can configure snapshot retention to a contractual shorter window; Private deployments follow customer backup policy.

- Debug traces and telemetry: traces are sampled and scrubbed; debugging snapshots include minimal context and are time-limited (default 30 days). We can implement a 7-day policy for both request logs and debug traces for enterprise customers under a contract/commitment.

- Evidence: attestation is standard; for extra assurance we can provide a signed addendum that enumerates the technical controls and a short checklist showing how deletion was executed for any future erase request. SOC 2 report covers access controls, change management, and encryption-in-transit/at-rest.

If you want, we can add a sentence in the attestation that explicitly states: "Redwood will not use customer content to train or fine-tune production or research models unless explicitly agreed in writing by the customer."
